title: Photosynthesis Knowledge Base
summary: Comprehensive revision knowledge base covering the overall equation, chloroplast structure, light-dependent and light-independent stages, limiting factors, uses of glucose, and common misconceptions in photosynthesis.

knowledge.text: The overall equation for photosynthesis is 6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2.
Photosynthesis uses light energy absorbed by chlorophyll.
Chloroplast: The organelle where photosynthesis takes place.
Thylakoid membranes: Internal chloroplast membranes stacked into grana that hold chlorophyll.
Grana: Stacks of thylakoid membranes inside the chloroplast.
Stroma: The fluid surrounding the thylakoid membranes in the chloroplast.
The light-dependent reaction occurs in the thylakoid membranes.
During the light-dependent reaction, light excites electrons in chlorophyll within photosystems II and I.
Photolysis: The splitting of water into H+ ions, electrons, and oxygen using light energy.
Oxygen is released as a by-product of photolysis during the light-dependent reaction.
The electron transport chain pumps H+ ions across the thylakoid membrane.
The flow of H+ ions drives ATP synthase to produce ATP, a process known as photophosphorylation.
NADP is reduced to NADPH during the light-dependent reaction.
Calvin cycle: The light-independent reaction of photosynthesis occurring in the stroma.
The light-independent reaction takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.
RuBisCO: The enzyme that fixes carbon dioxide onto ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP).
RuBP is a 5-carbon (5C) molecule.
RuBisCO fixes CO2 onto RuBP (5C) to produce two molecules of glycerate 3-phosphate (GP).
Glycerate 3-phosphate (GP) is a 3-carbon (3C) molecule.
GP is reduced to triose phosphate (TP) using ATP and NADPH from the light-dependent reaction.
Some triose phosphate (TP) is used to synthesise glucose and other organic molecules.
Most triose phosphate (TP) is used to regenerate RuBP, requiring ATP.
The three main limiting factors of photosynthesis are light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature.
Excessively high temperatures denature photosynthetic enzymes, reducing the rate of photosynthesis.
The factor in shortest supply is the limiting factor that determines and limits the rate of photosynthesis.
Glucose produced in photosynthesis is used in respiration to release energy.
Glucose can be converted into insoluble starch for storage.
Glucose is converted into cellulose to build plant cell walls.
Glucose is converted into sucrose for transport around the plant.
Glucose is combined with nitrates to produce amino acids and proteins.
Plants respire continuously, both day and night.
The oxygen released in photosynthesis originates from the splitting of water, not from carbon dioxide.
The Calvin cycle does not directly require light, but it depends on the products (ATP and NADPH) of the light-dependent reaction.

intro.text: The overall equation for photosynthesis is 6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2. Photosynthesis uses light energy absorbed by chlorophyll.
Chloroplast is the organelle where photosynthesis takes place. Inside, thylakoid membranes are stacked into grana holding chlorophyll, all surrounded by fluid called the stroma.

The light-dependent reaction occurs in the thylakoid membranes. Light excites electrons in chlorophyll within photosystems II and I. Photolysis splits water into H+ ions, electrons, and oxygen using light energy.
The electron transport chain pumps H+ ions across the thylakoid membrane. The flow drives ATP synthase to produce ATP via photophosphorylation, and NADP is reduced to NADPH.
The Calvin cycle is the light-independent reaction occurring in the stroma. It does not directly require light, but depends on ATP and NADPH from the light-dependent reaction.
RuBisCO fixes carbon dioxide onto a 5-carbon RuBP to produce two molecules of 3-carbon glycerate 3-phosphate. GP is reduced to triose phosphate using ATP and NADPH.
Some triose phosphate makes glucose for respiration, starch, cellulose, sucrose, or amino acids. Limiting factors include light, CO2, and temperature, with high heat denaturing enzymes.

clues.label: Overall Equation
clues.why: This is the correct overall chemical equation for photosynthesis.

clues.label: Oxygen Source
clues.claim: Released oxygen originates from splitting carbon dioxide
clues.why: Oxygen released originates from the splitting of water during photolysis, not carbon dioxide.

clues.label: Grana Structure
clues.claim: Grana are stacks of thylakoid membranes
clues.why: Grana are indeed stacks of thylakoid membranes inside the chloroplast.

clues.label: Temperature Effect
clues.claim: Excessively high temperatures denature photosynthetic enzymes
clues.why: Very high temperatures denature enzymes, reducing the photosynthetic rate.

clues.label: Plant Respiration
clues.claim: Plants only respire during the night
clues.why: Plants respire continuously, both day and night.

clues.label: Glucose Uses
clues.claim: Glucose can convert to starch, cellulose, and sucrose
clues.why: Glucose is converted into insoluble starch for storage, cellulose for walls, and sucrose for transport.
